key_insight: High accuracy on ordered, pre-aligned time series tasks does not establish that LLMs use timestamps to connect observations with real-world events.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate timestamp dependence and event-series alignment explicitly before trusting LLMs to reason over time series and external events.
method: Treat timestamps as indices connecting observations and events to shared world states.
Distinguish temporal causal structure, time semantics, and event-series alignment.
Apply controlled interventions to separate timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts.
evidence_signal: Across 310 questions from two tasks, accuracy could remain high with relative offsets or no timestamps, while disrupted event-series alignment induced systematic failures.
watch_item: Results cover two tasks; broader generalization requires testing on more domains and less curated temporal contexts.
paper_title: Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning
